info.title: PE Solar API
info.description:
Production-grade solar position, irradiance, and HVAC surface/shading calculation API. Powered by pvlib-python (NREL SPA algorithm).

**Citation:** W. F. Holmgren, C. W. Hansen, and M. A. Mikofski, "pvlib python: a python package for modeling solar energy systems," Journal of Open Source Software, 3(29), 884, (2018). https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.00884

post.description: Calculate solar zenith, azimuth, elevation, and apparent angles for a given location and timezone-aware datetime. Uses the NREL SPA algorithm via pvlib (accuracy ±0.0003°).

422.description: Validation error — e.g. timezone-naive datetime, out-of-range coordinates.

post.description: Calculate solar noon (transit) time and the offset from clock noon for a given location and date.

post.summary: Calculate sunrise, sunset, and day length
post.description: Calculate sunrise, sunset, and day length for a given location and date. Handles polar day/night conditions.

Calculate sun path over a time range — batch version of /position. Returns an array of solar position data points at the specified interval. Maximum 8760 data points (one year hourly). Returns 422 if the requested range exceeds the maximum.

422.description: Validation error or batch size exceeded. Maximum 8760 data points.

get.summary: Get solar declination and equation of time
get.description: Low-level building block: solar declination angle and equation of time for a given date or day-of-year. Uses Spencer (1971) formulas via pvlib.

post.description: Calculate clear-sky direct, diffuse, and global irradiance on a horizontal or tilted surface. Uses Ineichen/Perez clear-sky model for DNI/DHI/GHI, then pvlib's isotropic transposition model for plane-of-array (POA) values. Linke turbidity defaults to pvlib's climatological lookup if not provided.

post.summary: Calculate clear-sky irradiance with explicit model choice
post.description:
Thin wrapper exposing clear-sky model choice explicitly. For engineers who want a specific ASHRAE-adjacent clear-sky method rather than the opinionated default in /irradiance.

Available models:
- **ineichen**: Ineichen/Perez (default) — high accuracy, requires Linke turbidity
- **haurwitz**: Haurwitz (1945) — simple, no turbidity needed, GHI only
- **simplified_solis**: Simplified Solis — uses AOD and precipitable water

post.summary: Calculate angle of incidence on a tilted surface
post.description: Calculate the angle between the sun's direct beam and the normal to a tilted/oriented surface (wall, window, roof). Essential for computing direct irradiance on non-horizontal surfaces. Wraps pvlib.irradiance.aoi().

post.summary: Calculate shading from overhangs, fins, or obstructions
post.description:
Calculate shading mask/cutoff angle from overhangs, fins, or adjacent obstructions. Returns profile angle, horizontal shadow angle, shading factor, and whether the surface is shaded.

**Note:** This is custom domain logic built on top of pvlib's solar position output — pvlib does not include a building-shading-mask model. The shading geometry uses standard ASHRAE profile angle and horizontal shadow angle formulas.

post.summary: Calculate solar heat gain through a window
post.description:
End-to-end solar heat gain through a window: composes irradiance + shading + SHGC (Solar Heat Gain Coefficient) into one practical HVAC deliverable.

Formula: `heat_gain = POA_irradiance × area × SHGC × (1 - shading_factor)`

Returns results in both Watts and BTU/h. Optionally applies shading from overhangs/fins if obstruction geometry is provided.
